newsitem.title: USA: Bear bites hiker in Denali National Park.
newsitem.headline: Bear bites hiker in Denali National Park.

text.p: A hiker in Denali National Park was bitten and slightly injured by a grizzly bear Thursday, officials said.
The hiker, a 20-year-old woman, was charged by the female bear in a backcountry part of the sprawling national park, park officials said.
The hiker had been making noise to avoid surprising the area's bears, as is recommended, but was charged nonetheless, park officials said.

The woman then curled up into a foetal position and went limp, as recommended by experts, to appear dead and not a threat to the animal, the Park Service said. The grizzly bit her right hand, pawed lightly at her head and pack, then departed, officials said.
The hiker, whose name was withheld, was treated at a local clinic.
It was the first bear-caused injury in Denali since 1988, park officials said. No human has ever been killed by a bear in the park, Denali officials said.

Wildlife management technicians at the park closed the backcountry unit temporarily, but have no plans to remove the bear from the site because the confrontation appeared to be a case of a bear sow defending its cubs, officials said.
